product_scope.problem_statement: The current phase-2 state machine mixes operational orchestration with fragile payload handling and conflicts with the intended separation of responsibilities between the business consumer and the operational workflow.
product_scope.goal: Refactor the state machine so it becomes the single owner of operational history, lifecycle progression, idempotency fail-fast behavior, retry policy, and final persistence, while the consumer Lambda remains pure business execution.
success_outcomes: The state machine owns the operational lifecycle from lock acquisition to final closure.
The consumer Lambda no longer owns persistence of success or failure results.
Duplicate work items are stopped early through fail-fast idempotency.
Transient provider failures are retried with exponential backoff and full jitter.
Terminal failures are closed immediately without retry.
Final operational evidence is persisted in one consistent path.

in_scope: Refactor of the AWS Step Functions workflow for phase 2.
Pending record lifecycle transition from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED or FAILED.
Retry policy for transient provider failures with exponential backoff and full jitter.
Immediate failure capture for terminal provider errors.
Final persistence of success and failure evidence by the state machine.
Use of native DynamoDB Step Functions integrations whenever possible.
out_of_scope: Changes to the producer dispatch model.
Changes to SQS FIFO provider isolation.
Business rule changes in provider API classification beyond the existing transient versus terminal distinction.

actors.name: Producer
actors.description: Dispatches eligible work items into the provider-isolated FIFO queue.

actors.name: Orchestrator Lambda
actors.description: Starts one state machine execution per work item.

actors.name: State Machine
actors.description: Owns operational flow, retries, lifecycle transitions, idempotency, and final persistence.

actors.name: Consumer Lambda
actors.description: Executes the provider API call and returns business success or failure information.

actors.name: Technical Reviewer
actors.description: Validates that orchestration concerns are separated cleanly from business execution.

user_journeys.name: Successful work item closes through the success path
steps: A work item starts its orchestration execution.
The state machine acquires the idempotency lock.
The state machine marks the pending record as in progress.
The state machine persists final success evidence, closes the idempotency record, and marks the pending record as completed.

user_journeys.name: Transient provider failure is retried with resilience controls
steps: The provider returns a transient failure.
The state machine retries the consumer Lambda using exponential backoff and full jitter.
The work item eventually succeeds or exhausts retry attempts.
The state machine persists the final outcome and closes the lifecycle.

user_journeys.name: Terminal provider failure closes immediately
steps: The provider returns a terminal failure.
The state machine stops retrying immediately.
The state machine persists failure evidence and marks the work item as failed.

user_journeys.name: Duplicate work item ends as fail-fast duplicate
steps: A duplicate logical work item starts execution.
The state machine fails to acquire the idempotency lock or cannot claim the pending record.
The execution ends without invoking the provider Lambda a second time.

use_cases.title: Acquire duplicate protection before business execution
use_cases.description: The workflow must claim a logical work item before any provider call is attempted.

use_cases.title: Advance the pending record lifecycle
use_cases.description: The workflow must reflect operational progress in the pending record state.

use_cases.title: Retry transient provider failures with jittered backoff
use_cases.description: The workflow must absorb temporary provider instability without causing thundering herd behavior.

use_cases.title: Stop terminal failures immediately
use_cases.description: The workflow must avoid retrying failures that are not recoverable by repetition.

use_cases.title: Persist final evidence from the orchestration layer
use_cases.description: The workflow must be the single owner of final success and failure records.

business_rules.rule: The state machine must remain operational only and must not embed provider business rules beyond already-classified transient versus terminal outcomes.
The consumer Lambda must not own final persistence in the results table.
A work item must acquire idempotency protection before any provider execution.
A duplicate work item must stop early without a second independent provider call.
A transient failure must be retried with exponential backoff and full jitter.
A terminal failure must not be retried.
The pending record lifecycle must reflect PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, and FAILED.
Final success and failure evidence must be written by the orchestration workflow, not by the business Lambda.

functional_requirements.title: Idempotency lock acquisition
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must attempt conditional acquisition of a lock for each logical work item before invoking the consumer Lambda.

functional_requirements.title: Fail-fast duplicate handling
functional_requirements.statement: If the logical work item is already claimed, the workflow must finish without a second business execution.

functional_requirements.title: Pending record in-progress transition
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must transition the pending record from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS before business execution.

functional_requirements.title: Transient retry behavior
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must retry transient provider failures using exponential backoff with full jitter.

functional_requirements.title: Terminal failure behavior
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must route terminal provider failures directly to final failure closure.

functional_requirements.title: Success persistence ownership
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must persist final success evidence after a successful consumer execution.

functional_requirements.title: Failure persistence ownership
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must persist final failure evidence after a terminal failure or exhausted transient retries.

functional_requirements.title: Pending record final closure
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must mark the pending record as COMPLETED on success and FAILED on terminal or exhausted failure.

acceptance_criteria.given: A new work item starts execution
acceptance_criteria.then: It must attempt idempotency lock acquisition before any provider call.

acceptance_criteria.when: The workflow handles the work item
acceptance_criteria.then: It must end without invoking the consumer Lambda again.
The pending record must transition to IN_PROGRESS.

acceptance_criteria.when: The workflow closes the work item
acceptance_criteria.then: It must persist success evidence, complete the idempotency record, and mark the pending record as COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria.given: The consumer Lambda reports a transient provider failure
acceptance_criteria.then: It must retry with exponential backoff and full jitter.

acceptance_criteria.when: The workflow closes the work item
acceptance_criteria.then: It must persist final failure evidence and mark the pending record as FAILED.

acceptance_criteria.given: The consumer Lambda reports a terminal provider failure
acceptance_criteria.then: It must skip retry and close directly through the failure path.

acceptance_criteria.when: They compare the state machine and the consumer
acceptance_criteria.then: They must see that persistence ownership belongs to the state machine and business execution belongs to the consumer Lambda.

assumptions: Provider error classification continues to be produced by the consumer Lambda as transient versus terminal outcomes.
SQS FIFO remains the source of same-provider isolation and is not redefined by this refactor.
Operational duplicate handling can finish as a no-op successful termination rather than a failed execution.
This feature is a focused refactor inside phase 2, not a new phase with new product scope.

open_questions.question: Should duplicate terminations write explicit audit evidence to tapi-results, or is idempotency plus execution history sufficient?
open_questions.resolved_as: Do not persist duplicate outcomes in tapi-results; treat them as operational no-op completions.
